newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner - new phone bank will break even in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner - new phone bank will break even in 5 yrs.

text.p: Dresdner Bank AG said on Wednesday it expected its new telephone banking subsidiary to reach the break-even level in the next five years.
Dresdner plans to set up the bank in the second half of 1997, becoming the last of Germany's top five commercial banks to do so.
Dresdner-new phone bank will break even in 5 yrs

The bank would have an after-tax return of 15 percent on average in its first 10 years, management board member Heinz-Joerg Platzek told a news conference. That prediction factored in start-up losses in the initial years, Platzek said.
The subsidiary will start with 170 staff.
Platzek predicted the bank will gain 500,000 custmers within the next 10 years and offer a comprehensive range of services. Its name has not been decided yet.

Dresdner rivals Deutsche Bank AG, Commerzbank AG Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG have all set up telephone banking units in a bid to woo customers and make their cost-laden retail banking businesses more efficient.
